sources.entry: Ratelog - Movie tracker and rating app (alternative to Letterboxd). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Ratelog is a self-hostable web app for searching movies and TV shows via TMDB, rating them across five categories, and building ranked top lists, positioned as an alternative to Letterboxd.
summary.what_it_does: Ratelog lets users search movies and TV shows through the TMDB API and rate each title from 1 to 10 in 0.25 steps across five categories: Directing, Cinematography, Acting, Soundtrack, and Screenplay. It computes an automatic average across those categories and allows one rating per title, which can be deleted and redone. Users can generate top lists for movies and TV shows, filterable by year and category with configurable limits, and create custom lists. Follows track upcoming releases on a premieres page grouped by Released, Upcoming, and No Date. It supports multi-user accounts with USER, ADMIN, and SUPERADMIN roles, and can import ratings and watchlists from a Letterboxd export. It is a PWA that can be installed on mobile devices.
use_cases: track movies and TV shows I have watched
create ranked top lists of movies
self-host a movie rating app for my household
how_to_run: Edit .env to set PORT, POSTGRES_* variables and other settings
Log in as bootstrap admin (admin / admin) and change the password immediately
Set the TMDB API key in Configuración > General (/admin/configuration)
stack: PostgreSQL 17 (README also mentions PostgreSQL 18 in compose services)
notable: Multi-category rating system with automatic averaging across five categories
Letterboxd import for ratings and watchlist
Role hierarchy (USER, ADMIN, SUPERADMIN) with an admin dashboard
Progressive Web App install instructions for iOS and Android
caveats: Requires a TMDB API key; search, trending and detail features do not work without it
Mobile access requires the app to be reachable from the device (same network, tunnel or VPN)
Default bootstrap admin credentials (admin/admin) must be changed after first login
README notes it is a man-driven project heavily supported by AI-assisted development; contributing guide is marked 'coming soon'
